guardrails.no_p_hacking: Each is registered ONCE with fixed parameters before running. Failures are reported and the variant dropped; no parameter sweeps.
guardrails.multiple_testing_disclosure: These are the 11th-13th variants on the same data. Accumulated searching is itself a statistical cost: the more variants tried, the more likely one looks good by luck. Treat any single winner with more suspicion than the first result, and confirm on real-option data before promoting anything.
guardrails.same_deviations: Proxied IV, constant-IV repricing, model credit -> UPPER BOUND.

trial_accounting.note: same universe/structures; these are policy refinements, but see the multiple-testing disclosure.

promotion: No promotion. SHADOW research. v5 stays live; v10 remains the leading candidate unless one of these clearly beats it.
objective: RISK MANAGEMENT lever (never tested): add a hard STOP-LOSS to the exit policy. Every variant so far has an upside target (50% of credit) but NO downside stop -- losers run to near-max width. Exit when the position's marked loss reaches 2x the credit received.
philosophy: All prior variants tuned ENTRY selection. This tunes EXIT risk. The book's core defect is asymmetry: 81% win rate but avg loss 3-6x avg win (2022: avg win $58 vs avg loss $192). A stop truncates the left tail directly instead of trying to predict it.
change: In simulate_exit, if the cost to close reaches 3x the entry credit (i.e. a realized loss of 2x credit), exit there. The 50% profit target and expiry fallback are unchanged.
predictions: 2022 loss shrinks materially vs v10's -$2,880 (the stop caps the bear tail)
overall win rate FALLS (stops convert would-be recoveries into realized losses)
cluster-adjusted max drawdown improves vs v10's -$709
total PnL may fall -- if it does, the stop bought drawdown reduction at a cost, and that is the honest tradeoff to weigh
risk: Premium-selling stops are known to whipsaw: a spread can breach a stop and still expire worthless. A worse total with a better drawdown is a plausible and acceptable finding.
